quarterly_data.quarter: Air Liquide IR presentation: BEYOND strategic plan (10-05-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: BEYOND Capital Markets Day deck (dated 5 October 2026), Electronics: Air Liquide targets Electronics sales growing from €2.5bn in 2025 to >€4bn in 2030 (>+10% sales CAGR, including the scope impact of the DIG acquisition), with >50% of the growth already secured; the Electronics backlog rose +80% from €1.4bn (H1 24) to €2.5bn (H1 26), which is 40% of the H1 2026 Group backlog and is made of 26 projects (>€10m of investment) including 11 large projects >€100m capex in 11 countries in strategic semiconductor hubs; Electronics is ~50% of 12-month Group investment opportunities. Carrier gases were 51% of EL sales in 2025 (long-term contracts, energy pass-through, larger units to supply mega fabs, >20 project start-ups between 2026 and 2028); advanced materials were 17% of EL sales in 2025 and are targeted at >+30% sales CAGR 2026-2030, with Air Liquide claiming to be first-to-market with molybdenum precursor solutions for next-generation chips. In Asia it plans ~€3bn of carrier-gas investment decisions over 2026-2030 and expects Electronics to rise from 29% (2020) to 40% (2030) of Asia sales; in the Americas it cites an EL gases market >x2 by 2030 and >5 carrier-gas major project start-ups.
quarterly_data.figure: EL backlog €2.5bn (H1 26, +80%); EL sales €2.5bn (2025) to >€4bn (2030); advanced materials >+30% CAGR; Asia carrier-gas investment ~€3bn

quarterly_data.quarter: Air Liquide IR presentation: BEYOND strategic plan (10-05-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: BEYOND Capital Markets Day deck, indicative split of the +5% ±1% sales CAGR (2026-2030, ex FX and energy): Industrial Merchant +4-6%, Large Industries +1-3%, Electronics >+10%, Healthcare +4-6%; by geography Americas +5-6% (40% of 2025 Gas & Services sales), EMEA +2-3% (41%) and Asia +8-9% (19%). Capital allocation of >€40bn includes €22-25bn of investments in the business (including bolt-on acquisitions) over 2026-2030 and €24bn of industrial investment decisions; Energy Transition has a €2.2bn backlog (H1 2026) with 8 major projects >€100m capex, €2.5bn of selective investment decisions over 2026-2030 and an additional >€700m of sales by 2030. Operational KPIs by 2030: +10% asset loading, -15% capex on new plants, >3x fewer production incidents, +50% packaged-gas productivity. Headcount fell from 67,800 (FY 2023) to 64,700 (H1 2026), -4,000 (-6%) excluding scope. Assumptions: 1.19 USD for 1€, ~+2% industrial production CAGR, end-2025 energy prices. The deck states these drivers and levers are not targets.
quarterly_data.figure: Electronics >+10%, Asia +8-9%, Americas +5-6%, EMEA +2-3% sales CAGR; investments €22-25bn; Energy Transition backlog €2.2bn
